nodes.label: publish workflow
nodes.rationale: Fires when a GitHub Release is published, with a workflow_dispatch fallback because a release-event run uses the workflow file at the tag's commit, so a workflow bug cannot be fixed and re-run through the release event alone. Runs are serialised rather than cancelled — an in-flight npm publish is the last thing to interrupt — because the version guard is a check-then-act that two overlapping runs would both pass.

nodes.label: publish job
nodes.rationale: Typecheck, test and build are deliberately not separate steps: npm publish runs prepublishOnly on the same Bun toolchain immediately before publishing, so explicit steps would run the whole suite twice. The DevTools UI toolchain is installed anyway, because prepublishOnly reaches it and without that the publish would fail at the last possible moment — after the tag and the GitHub Release already exist.

nodes.label: npm Trusted Publishing via OIDC
nodes.rationale: No long-lived NPM_TOKEN: the workflow exchanges its short-lived OIDC token for a one-shot publish token at runtime, and --provenance signs via the same id-token. Requires npm >= 11.5.1, which Node 24 already bundles.

nodes.label: SHA-pinned actions (#585)
nodes.rationale: The actions run in the same job that holds id-token: write, so an action author — or anyone who compromises their account — who repoints a mutable tag executes code next to a credential that can publish actor-ts to npm with provenance. A SHA cannot be repointed; the trailing # vX.Y.Z comment is what keeps Dependabot updating the pin.

nodes.label: CycloneDX SBOM job
nodes.rationale: --provenance answers who built the tarball and says nothing about what is inside the closure. The install is what makes the SBOM accurate: a bill of materials assembled from unresolved ranges is worse than none, because it looks authoritative and names versions nobody shipped. Ten non-shipping manifests are deleted before the scan, since leaving them in would make the document actively misleading about which advisories affect a release.

nodes.label: attach-SBOM job
nodes.rationale: Split from the generating job on purpose, not for style: a single job would hold a contents: write credential while running the postinstall scripts of the entire dependency tree, which WorkflowHygiene.test.ts fails on since #622. No checkout and no install here — that is the point of the split. --clobber so the manual re-run fallback does not die on 'asset already exists'.
